name: Roll Cage
description: Weld-in 6-point+ road-race roll cage (main hoop, front hoop, halo/roof rails, roof X, diagonals, harness bar, backstays, door bars, dash bar, optional strut-tower down-bars) with mounting plates, gussets and SFI 45.1 padding. Tube size per NASA CCR/SCCA GCR weight tables (1.75 x .120 DOM for a ~3,500 lb Camaro).

components.name: Main hoop (B-pillar hoop)
components.description: Single-piece, near-vertical hoop immediately behind the front seats that carries roll-over loads to the floor. It is the backbone of the cage: the harness bar, main-hoop diagonal, backstays, roof rails and door bars all terminate on it. Must be one continuous bent tube (no joints) with the near-vertical legs as close as possible to the B-pillar inner panels and only one bend in each leg.
components.location: Spans the cabin at the B-pillar, x ≈ 2.15–2.18; feet welded to plates on the floor/rocker junction (z ≈ ±0.66), top tucked under the roof skin at y ≈ 1.27.

factory.name: None – production Camaro has no roll structure (CMS Performance offers a Gen 6 bolt-in roll bar as a street/HPDE step)
factory.notes: CMS Gen 6 bar: 1.75 x .095 Docol R8, one-piece main hoop/kicker, ~51 lb – a roll BAR, not a road-race cage.

raceOptions.name: Custom weld-in cage, 1.75 x .120 DOM (NASA 3,001–4,000 lb bracket)
raceOptions.brand: Local chassis shop / S&W Race Cars / Autopower (custom)
raceOptions.notes: Gen 6 race weight w/o driver & fuel ≈ 3,400–3,700 lb → 1.75 x .120 per NASA CCR table quoted in the sources; SCCA 2,700 lb+ allows 1.50 x .120 / 1.75 x .095 / 2.00 x .080.

raceOptions.name: Chromoly 4130 1.75 x .095 or .120 (normalized)
raceOptions.notes: Lighter; requires TIG and qualified welder; SCCA forbids mixing alloy and mild tube in one cage.

raceOptions.name: FIA build-to-spec main hoop 45 x 2.5 mm or 50 x 2.0 mm (350 N/mm² min)
raceOptions.notes: For FIA-style events; note post-2017 homologated cars must use homologated/certified cages.

specs.Tube: 1.750 in OD x 0.120 in wall DOM (SAE 1020/1026) or 4130 seamless
specs.Helmet clearance: SCCA: ≥ 2 in above helmet (cars w/o roof); NASA: pad within reach of helmet

hardware.item: TIG/MIG weld joint – full 360° fillet, full penetration
hardware.spec: ER70S-2/ER70S-6 (mild/DOM) or ER80S-D2 / ER70S-2 per 4130 practice
hardware.notes: FIA 253-8.3.4: all welds full penetration around the whole tube perimeter, preferably gas-shielded arc. Do not mix mild and alloy tube (SCCA).

hardware.item: Wall-thickness inspection hole
hardware.spec: 3/16–1/4 in drilled hole in non-critical straight section
hardware.notes: SCCA requires an inspection hole in front and main hoops and one supplemental brace (or non-invasive ultrasonic measurement logged in the logbook).

installNotes: Strip cabin to bare metal (interior.strip-and-deadener-removal) and seam-weld if planned before fitting tubes.
Fit seat, steering column and pedal box mock-up first so the hoop clears the driver helmet with the seat in final position.
Tack mounting plates, then notch-fit the hoop through the roof line as high and close to the B-pillar as possible.
Check driver helmet clearance with driver seated + helmet + FHR before final welding.
Final-weld in alternating short beads to minimize distortion; weld plates 360°.
Drill inspection hole per SCCA, mark with paint pen, record wall thickness in logbook.
inspection: Check all welds for cracks (dye-penetrant after any impact).
Inspect foot plates and surrounding floor for cracking/tearing.
Verify padding still secured where helmet can contact.

hardware.notes: SCCA requires an inspection hole in front and main hoops and one supplemental brace (or non-invasive ultrasonic measurement logged in the logbook).

installNotes: Remove headliner, A-pillar trims, and pull the dash forward or out for access (interior.dash).
Bend to follow the A-pillar/windshield header; keep tube within ~1 in of the pillar to preserve visibility and head room.
Check that driver eye line and windshield wiper/defrost (if retained) are not blocked.
Tie in to roof rails (halo) at the header corners; gusset both corners.
inspection: Check A-pillar bar welds and header corner gussets.
Look for windshield cracks originating near the header (body flex indicator).

components.name: Harness (shoulder-belt) bar
components.description: Horizontal tube across the main hoop at shoulder-belt height. The shoulder belts wrap around it (3-bar slide) so the belts leave the shoulders at 0° to about −20° to horizontal per harness maker guidance. Doubles as the main-hoop horizontal brace.
components.location: Across the main hoop, x ≈ 2.155, y ≈ 0.84, full width z ±0.70.

specs.Tube: 1.750 in OD x 0.120 in wall DOM (SAE 1020/1026) or 4130 seamless
specs.Height: Set so shoulder belts leave shoulders 0° to −20° (FIA allows 10°–45° down from backrest rim; 10° recommended)
specs.Distance from seat back: Schroth: ≤ 200 mm (8 in) ideal for FHR

hardware.item: TIG/MIG weld joint – full 360° fillet, full penetration
hardware.spec: ER70S-2/ER70S-6 (mild/DOM) or ER80S-D2 / ER70S-2 per 4130 practice

installNotes: Install the seat FIRST and measure driver shoulder height in the seat with helmet and FHR.
Position bar so belt angle is between 0° and −20° from horizontal at the shoulder; never route belts upward.
Keep at least 90 mm between seatback and harness pivot point (FIA 253-61-c per Lefrog).
Do not drill the bar for eyebolts unless the cage builder certifies it.
inspection: Look for webbing abrasion marks / sharp weld spatter where belts wrap.

components.name: Main hoop mounting plates (floor/rocker)
components.description: Steel plates welded to the floor/rocker junction under each main-hoop leg. They spread roll-over load into the unibody and give the tube a 360° weld land. Often bent to wrap up the rocker inner wall (multi-plane plates are allowed).
components.location: Under main hoop feet, x ≈ 2.15, y ≈ 0.19, z ±0.66 (on floor where it meets the inner rocker/B-pillar base).

specs.Material: 0.125 in (3.2 mm) mild steel plate typical
specs.NASA size: 9–100 in² each, each side 2–12 in, ≥ 0.080 in if welded (CCR 15.6.14 as quoted)
specs.SCCA L3: welded 0.080–0.25 in; bolted ≥ tube wall + backing plate, ≤ 15 in any side

hardware.item: Plate-to-chassis weld (360° perimeter)
hardware.spec: MIG/TIG stitch then continuous perimeter weld to floor/rocker
hardware.notes: NASA: one mounting point per plate, 360° tube-to-plate weld. SCCA L3: welded plates 0.080–0.25 in thick.

hardware.item: Bolt-in alternative: plate bolts
hardware.spec: 3/8-16 UNC hex bolt + nyloc + hardened washers, through backing plate of equal size/thickness
hardware.notes: SCCA L3 bolted plates need backing plate of equal size & thickness, ≥ 3 bolts typical; FIA requires ≥ 3 × M8 8.8 per foot on a 3 mm/120 cm² reinforcement plate (M8 8.8 ≈ 25 N·m). Torque is standard dry Grade 8 chart value. Checked 2026-10: no cage-maker or FIA/SFI torque is published. 44 ft-lb sits within standard dry SAE Grade 8 3/8-16 values (40-52 ft-lb, Quadratec / Melling-AERA charts). Remains typical.

installNotes: Grind e-coat/sealer to bare metal; plates should sit flat with full contact.
Weld plates to chassis before final tube weld so the tube can be welded 360° to the plate.
Avoid placing plates over seam-sealed joints without first welding the seam.
inspection: Check for floor cracking around plate edges.
